name: bench50
description: Video-to-MuJoCo benchmark: 25 PhysInOne + 25 Physion v1.5 scenes. Every video is on the real-time axis: one video second is one second of physics with g = 9.81 m/s^2 in the GT metres.

criteria.scope: PhysInOne (SinglePhysics, Train split) + Physion v1.5 (test split), 25 scenes each
physical_plausibility: PhysInOne movers: linear damping <= 0.05 and angular damping <= 0.5 (Chaos defaults 0.01/0); no zero mass
GT friction deceleration <= 1 g (PhysInOne) / stops faster than 0.6 g are collisions (Physion mu_dyn 0.25)
GT restitution <= 0.95; clip gravity consistent with the dataset value (2.25 m/s^2 +-10 %) when measurable
colliding movers: GT mass / real-world prior (material or object class x hull volume from 4 GT depth views) agree within 3x across the movers
objects of fixed real size (balls, cans, bottles, Rubik cube) within 0.5-2x their real size
visual check of every scene: no floating spinning panels, no 2-6 m cannonballs/boulders, no 9.9 kg toy ball next to 10 kg boxes
Physion: one material for all objects (mu 0.4/0.25, e 0.4, masses proportional to volume); no rise of translational+potential energy
passive_reproducibility: all motion starts at the first frame: an initial velocity or gravity from rest (the task prompt forbids later pushes, motors and timed forces)
leading still frames before an invisible push / release are trimmed (first_frame: Physion dominoes 15, vase 5; PhysInOne pendulum release 18)
motor-accelerated spins (Accel*Spin) and catapults excluded; constant-rate spins kept (free flywheel)
fast spins that alias at the video frame rate (fan / windmill at ~1 rad per frame) excluded
evaluability: GT trajectories cover every video frame; video frames present (8 PhysInOne zips have none, 14 have no actor trajectories)
GT depth and segmentation for every frame (Physion drop_sidezone_box ships no _depth_cam0)
moving objects visible in camera 0 (>= 200 px in >= 50 % of frames for the main movers)
>= 1 GT physical-quantity item (initial speed, period, mass ratio, restitution, deceleration, spin rate / acceleration); spinning objects with visible texture (plain symmetric discs excluded)
no two scenes with identical GT motion (DoublePendulum bg071 variants differ only in material)
criteria.diversity: PhysInOne: 15 of 18 subclasses, 2 per subclass at most except pendulum/collision; Physion: all 7 categories, 1-4 subtypes each

timing.physinone: per clip: g_clip = median free-fall acceleration fitted on the GT actor transforms over GT time_seconds (10-sample windows; used when >= 5 windows agree within an IQR of 10 % of the median), else the dataset value 2.25 m/s^2; video rate = round(30 / sqrt(g_clip / 9.81), 4) fps
timing.physion_v15: 0.01 s per frame (100 fps), confirmed per clip from GT rotations vs angular velocities
timing.first_frame: the video starts at this source frame; source frame ids are kept in meta/<job_id>/timestamps.csv

encoding.ffmpeg: videos were made with FFmpeg 4.4.2 (Ubuntu 22.04, libx264 core 163 r3060); other versions may give different bytes (same frames and timestamps)
encoding.x264_threads: passed explicitly; x264 output depends on its thread count (these are the counts x264 chose automatically on the original 192-CPU host)
encoding.direct: source frames from first_frame -> ffmpeg -framerate R -start_number 0 -i %06d.<jpg|png> -an -c:v libx264 -threads T -preset veryfast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -vf pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2 -r R -movflags +faststart; R = 100 (Physion) or N/10000 (PhysInOne)
encoding.two_step: step 1 (all source frames at 30 fps): ffmpeg -threads 1 -framerate 30.0 -start_number 0 -i %06d.<jpg|png> -an -c:v libx264 -threads 1 -preset veryfast -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -vf pad=ceil(iw/2)*2:ceil(ih/2)*2 -movflags +faststart; step 2 (lossless, new timestamps): ffmpeg -i step1.mp4 -an -vf setpts=N/(R)/TB -r R -c:v libx264 -threads T -pix_fmt yuv420p -qp 0 -bf 0 -preset veryfast; for PhysInOne R = round(1 / (dt1 * sqrt(g_clip / 9.81)), 4) with dt1 the median step-1 frame interval as printed by ffprobe (0.033333 s)

physinone.files: scene ZIPs <category>/<scene>_trajectory.zip from the Hugging Face shard repos PhysInOneP01..P16 (index: vLAR/PhysInOne), each at a pinned revision, checked by the LFS sha256

physion_v15.license: not stated on the release page
physion_v15.files: HDF5 members <category>/<category>_all_movies/<sample>.hdf5 of the test-set ZIP per category, read by HTTP range requests and checked by the ZIP CRC32 and size
